### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19 and A20 were almost never executed (each in only about 1–2 in 200 traces); in the later window, A19 appears in about 46 in 100 traces and A20 in about 56 in 100 [OCC001, OCC002].
- In the earlier window, A40's outgoing transitions led almost exclusively to A25 (about 90 in 100); in the later window they lead mainly to A20 (about 53 in 100) and A19 (about 42 in 100), while the direct transition to A25 has nearly disappeared (about 0.5 in 100) [DIR003].
- In the later window, A19 and A20 each lead almost always to A25 (about 97 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions); their earlier outgoing profiles rest on only 1–2 observations and are weak [DIR001, DIR002].
- The distance from A40 to A25 shifted from mostly one step (about 90 in 100 cases) to mostly two steps (about 93 in 100) [LAG001].
- In the later window, A40 runs before A19 in about 45 in 100 traces and before A20 in about 56 in 100, and A19 runs before A25 in about 46 in 100 and A20 before A25 in about 55 in 100; in the earlier window, A25 and A40 essentially always appeared without A19 or A20 [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005].
- A19 and A20 behave as alternatives in the later window: at least one of them is present in about 99 in 100 traces, but they co-occur in only about 2 in 100 [REL001].
- A25 still occurs in every trace in both windows, and its position moved only slightly later (median from 0.36 to about 0.39 of the trace length) [POS003].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, an intermediate step — A19 or A20 — now runs between A40 and A25: A40, which previously led directly to A25 in about 90 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, now leads to A20 or A19 in about 95 in 100, and each of those in turn leads to A25 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions [DIR003, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001].

The relational evidence shows this directly and consistently: the A40-to-A25 distance moved from one step to two, the orderings A40 before A19/A20 and A19/A20 before A25 appear only in the later window, A19 and A20 are nearly mutually exclusive (consistent with one intermediate step chosen per case), and A25 itself remains universal and only slightly later, fitting a single added step rather than a broader reorganisation [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, POS003]. The volume of qualifying items (13, against roughly 0.46 expected if nothing had changed) also exceeds what an unchanged process typically produces [OCC001, OCC002, DIR003, LAG001].

Limitations: the earlier profiles of A19 and A20 rest on only 1–2 traces, so the evidence cannot distinguish a newly added activity from one that previously occurred extremely rarely, and it cannot show what determines whether A19 or A20 runs. An important competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that A19 and A20 were pre-existing but very rare paths whose usage rose sharply; the two-step route via them is nonetheless directly observed in the later window [OCC001, OCC002].

Other differences: small residual routing remains in the later window — A19 and A20 each send about 1 in 100 outgoing transitions to activities other than A25, and A40 keeps small shares to A02, A06 and A23 [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003].

Setup: 200 traces before, 200 traces after. Screening: 93 units tested, 0.46 items expected without change. We have 13 evidence items. That's many times larger than 0.46, so the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the "insufficient evidence" screening gate.

Now let's understand the behaviour.

OCC001: A19 participation before 0.005 (1 in 200 traces), after 0.455 (92 in 200 traces). Huge increase. Support before 1, after 92. So A19 was nearly absent before, appears in about 46 in 100 traces after.

OCC002: A20 participation before 0.01 (2 in 200), after 0.555 (111 in 200). Huge increase.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A19. Before: only A29 (1 observation, so 100% to A29). After: mostly A25 (96.7%), tiny shares to A14, A11, A43. Support before 1, after 92. So after, A19 almost always leads to A25.

DIR002: outgoing transitions of A20. Before: A21 0.5, A23 0.5 (2 observations). After: A25 96.4%, tiny shares to A10, A19, A04, A38. Support before 2, after 111. So after, A20 almost always leads to A25.

DIR003: outgoing transitions of A40. Before: mostly A25 (90.5%), small shares to A10 (2.5%), A02 (2%), A06 (2%), A08 (2%), A44 (0.5%), A04 (0.5%). After: A20 (53%), A19 (41.5%), A25 nearly gone (0.5%), A06 (3%), A23 (0.5%), A02 (1.5%). Support 200/200. So A40 used to lead mostly to A25; now it leads to A20 or A19.

POS001: A19 position. Before: support 0.005 (1 trace), mean position ~0.607. After: support 0.46, mean ~0.362, median ~0.357. So A19 now occurs around 36% of the way through the trace (earlier than the single before-observation at ~61%). Note: position shift alone doesn't show movement; but here it's mostly about new participation.

POS002: A20 position. Before: support 0.01, mean ~0.596. After: support 0.555, mean ~0.367. Similar.

POS003: A25 position. Support 1.0 both windows. Mean 0.379 → 0.402, median 0.36 → 0.389. Small shift later. Observed change 0.024, but empirical strength 0.995. Hmm, small but unusual. A25 occurs in all traces in both windows.

REL001: A19 & A20. Before: neither 98.5%, A_only 0.5%, B_only 1%. After: A_only 44%, B_only 53.5%, cooccurrence 2%, neither 0.5%. So before they almost never appeared; after, they each appear in about half of traces but rarely together (2 in 100). So A19 and A20 are largely alternatives to each other in the later window.

REL002: A19 & A25. Before: B_only (A25 only) 99.5%. After: cooccurrence 46%, B_only 54%, A_before_B 45.5%. So after, when A19 occurs, it occurs before A25 (A19 → A25), consistent with DIR001 (A19 leads to A25).

REL003: A19 & A40. Before: B_only (A40 only) 99.5%. After: cooccurrence 46%, B_only 54%, B_before_A 45%. So A40 before A19. Consistent with DIR003: A40 → A19 (41.5%).

REL004: A20 & A25. Before: B_only 99%. After: cooccurrence 55.5%, B_only 44.5%, A_before_B 55%. So A20 before A25. Consistent with DIR002 (A20 → A25).

REL005: A20 & A40. Before: B_only 99%. After: cooccurrence 55.5%, B_before_A 55.5%. So A40 before A20. Consistent with DIR003 (A40 → A20, 53%).

LAG001: A40 → A25 lag. Before: lag 1 in 90.5%, lag 2 in 9.5%. After: lag 1 in 0.5%, lag 2 in 92.5%, lag 3 in 7%. So the direct A40→A25 edge (distance 1) nearly disappeared; now A40 reaches A25 at distance 2 (via an intermediate activity). Consistent with DIR003: A40 now goes to A19 or A20, which then go to A25. So an intermediate step was inserted between A40 and A25.

So the picture: Before, A40 was followed directly by A25 (in ~90 in 100 outgoing transitions of A40). A19 and A20 were essentially not executed (1 and 2 traces out of 200). After, A19 and A20 each appear in roughly half of traces (46 and 55.5 in 100), they are almost never in the same trace (2 in 100 co-occur), A40 now leads to A20 (53%) or A19 (41.5%) instead of directly to A25, and A19/A20 lead almost always to A25. The A40→A25 distance shifted from 1 step to 2 steps. A25 still occurs in all traces, its position shifted slightly later (median 0.36 → 0.389).

So the structural hypothesis: a new intermediate step was inserted between A40 and A25 — either A19 or A20 (as alternatives, since they rarely co-occur) now sits between A40 and A25. This is a placement/insertion hypothesis. The evidence is relational (REL, LAG, DIR successor changes) and direct: DIR003 shows A40's outgoing transitions changed from A25 to A19/A20; DIR001/DIR002 show A19/A20 lead to A25; LAG001 shows the A40→A25 distance moved from 1 to 2; REL002-005 confirm ordering (A40 before A19/A20, A19/A20 before A25).

This is strongly consistent and direct. Support level: Supported hypothesis.
